title: Age-specific distribution of serum thyrotropin and antithyroid antibodies in the US population: implications for the prevalence of subclinical hypothyroidism
journal: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism
population: NHANES III (1988 to 1994) participants without thyroid disease, analysed by age decile with and without antithyroid antibodies
authorConflicts: The authors have nothing to disclose.
result: Without thyroid disease, 10.6% of people aged 20 to 29 had TSH above 2.5 mIU/l, rising to 40% at age 80 or more, of whom 14.5% had TSH above 4.5 mIU/l. The 97.5th centile was 3.56 mIU/l at age 20 to 29 and 7.49 at 80 or more; the whole distribution, including the peak, shifted to higher TSH with age whether or not antibodies were present. Seventy percent of older people with TSH above 4.5 mIU/l were within their age-specific reference range. The authors state that lowering the upper limit to 2.5 mIU/l could designate as many as 35% of older people as hypothyroid.
